The missing middle ground is a lightweight form of polymorphism in the spirit of Hofmann and Pierce's type destructors and TypeScript's Parameters<T> and ReturnType<T>, which keeps the concise types of subtyping yet recovers the precision of parametricity. However, Hofmann and Pierce did not address contravariant positions such as function arguments, and TypeScript's utility types rely on the unsound `any` type.
  To address this gap, we present $F^{DR}_{<:}$, an extension of System $F_{<:}$ with first-class domain and range projection types, Dom(T) and Range(T), and an application rule that types f(x) from f : F and x : Dom(F) for an arbitrary type F. The demand that F be exposed as an arrow type is delayed from the definition site to the call site and discharged by the argument itself, as a value of type Dom(F) exists only when F is a subtype of an arrow type. A function type variable then needs no informative bound, only $<:$ Top, while its applications still type precisely, reaching the middle ground through a boundless quantification.
  We prove semantic type soundness and weak normalization by logical relations, where path selection delays a projection's interpretation until the underlying arrow type is resolved. The same machinery extends to product projections, which cooperate with domain and range in one system. All are mechanized in Rocq.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Online Job Assignment
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
Motivated primarily by applications in cloud computing, we study a simple, yet powerful, online allocation problem in which jobs of varying durations arrive over continuous time and must be assigned immediately and irrevocably to one of the available offline servers. Each server has a fixed initial capacity, with assigned jobs occupying one unit for their duration and releasing it upon completion. The algorithm earns a reward for each assignment upon completion. We consider a general heterogeneous setting where both the reward and duration of a job depend on the job-server pair. The objective of the online algorithm is to maximize the total collected reward, and remain competitive against an omniscient benchmark that knows all job arrivals in advance. Our main contribution is the design of a new online algorithm, termed Forward-Looking BALANCE (FLB), and using primal-dual framework to establish that it is (asymptotically) optimal-competitive.
  This meta-algorithm has two main primitives: (i) keeping track of the capacity used for each server at each time and applying a penalty function to this quantity, and (ii) adjusting the reward of assigning a job to a server by subtracting the total penalty of a particularly chosen subset of future times, in contrast to just looking at the current time. The FLB algorithm then assigns the arriving job to the server with the maximum adjusted reward. If R and D are the ratios of maximum over minimum rewards and durations, we show that the FLB algorithm obtains an asymptotic competitive ratio of ln(RD)+3lnln(max(R,D))+O(1). We further show this bound has optimal dependencies on all the parameters. Our main analysis combines a novel dual-fitting technique, which leverages the configuration LP benchmark for this problem, and a novel inductive argument to establish the capacity feasibility of the algorithm, which might be of independent interest.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Online Resource Allocation with Cancellations
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We initiate the study of two-sided online resource allocation with costly cancellations within the buyback model. Our focus is on edge-weighted online matching and several of its extensions. In our base matching model, nodes arrive online on one side and request offline resources on the other side. In contrast to the classic literature, in our model the decision maker can reclaim any fraction of an offline resource that was preallocated to an earlier online node. However, reclaiming a resource not only results in the loss of the previously allocated edge-weight but also incurs an additional penalty equal to a non-negative constant factor $f$ times the edge-weight. Parameterizing the problem by the buyback factor $f$, our main result is the development of optimal competitive algorithms for \emph{all possible values} of $f$ through a novel primal-dual family of algorithms in the fractional (or equivalently, large capacity) setting. We establish the optimality of our results by deriving separate lower bounds for both the small and large buyback factor regimes and showing that our primal-dual algorithm exactly matches these lower bounds by appropriately tuning a parameter as a function of $f$. Interestingly, our results reveal a phase transition: for the small buyback regime ($f < \frac{e-2}{2}$), the optimal competitive ratio is $\frac{e}{e-(1+f)}$, and for the large buyback regime ($f \geq \frac{e-2}{2}$), the competitive ratio is $-W_{-1}\left(\frac{-1}{e(1+f)}\right)$, where $W_{-1}$ is the non-principal branch of the Lambert $W$ function.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: A preliminary conference version of this work has appeared in the ACM Economics and Computations(EC) 2023 conference under the title "Online Resource Allocation with Buyback: Optimal Algorithms via Primal-Dual." ; An earlier version of this paper was distributed under the title "Online Matching with Cancellation Costs."

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Thin matrix products up to D <= N^0.172 and lossless reductions for 3SUM, Exact Triangle and APSP, with 3SUM over abelian groups and a dichotomy for coordinatewise problems
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Alman and Vassilevska Williams (arXiv:2610.06783) gave the first polynomial improvements over the textbook algorithms for 3SUM and APSP: deterministic algorithms with exponents 1.9992 for 3SUM, 2.9983 for Exact Triangle and 2.99942 for APSP. Their algorithm has two steps: a matrix theorem, computing N^2/sqrt(D) prescribed entries of the product of an N x D and a D x N integer matrix in time N^2/D^gamma, gamma > 0, when D <= N^eps, for every eps < 0.1204; and reductions from the three problems to the lopsided sparse triangle problem. We improve both. With Schönhage's five-term partial-product tensor, the matrix theorem holds for every eps < 0.172. The preprint's reductions keep a quarter of the matrix theorem's saving for 3SUM and a half for Exact Triangle and APSP; ours keep all of it, by calling the counting version of the triangle problem adaptively and building composite moduli one prime at a time. Together this gives deterministic 3SUM in n^{1.9945+o(1)}, and Exact Triangle, (min,+)-product and APSP in n^{2.9945+o(1)}. We also improve on the preprint's proof sketch for 3XOR and solve it deterministically in O(n^{1.99451}). Which other problems on three lists does the method make truly subquadratic? It solves 3SUM over F_p^d for every fixed prime p with 3XOR's exponents, and over every finite abelian group of exponent p^2, such as Z_4^d, in O(n^{1.99726}). For coordinatewise problems with a fixed relation P on every coordinate triple, a certified exhaustive computation shows that every Boolean P, and every functional P over three letters, either is the solution set of an equation over Z, F_2 or F_3, and the problem is then truly subquadratic, or has a gadget for Orthogonal Vectors, and the problem is then hard under the Orthogonal Vectors hypothesis. Over four letters, just four functional relations, up to symmetry, satisfy neither condition.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 130 pages. Lean formalisation and scripts: https://github.com/Majdoddin/formal-math

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Fast Forgiving Base64 Decoding with SIMD Instructions
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: On the Internet, we use the Base64 format to represent binary data (e.g., images or cryptographic keys) as text. The ES2026 JavaScript standard, following the WHATWG forgiving-base64 rules, requires decoders to ignore ASCII whitespace while rejecting other non-alphabet characters. Prior SIMD Base64 decoders assume whitespace-free input. We present a block-oriented decoding algorithm that removes whitespace inside the SIMD loop: clean 64-character blocks are decoded directly, while blocks with ignorable characters are compacted into a small stack buffer. We provide implementations for x64 (SSSE3 through AVX-512 VBMI2), ARM NEON, and LoongArch. Our C++ decoder reaches up to 94 GB/s on recent AMD Zen 5 processors. In Node.js 25, integration of our decoder raises Uint8Array.fromBase64 throughput by up to 6x compared with Node.js 19. The implementation has been adopted by major browsers and JavaScript runtimes.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Reportable Shortcuts with RLBWTs
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Backward search over a run-length compressed Burrows--Wheeler transform (RLBWT) takes one step per pattern character, even when long stretches of the pattern match material that recurs throughout a highly repetitive collection. We describe \emph{shortcuts}: for a precomputed set of pairs $(α,β)$ of strings, a backward search that has just matched $β$ and finds $α$ immediately to its left in the pattern can cross $α$ in one step. Since a shortcut is taken only after its pair has been recognized in the pattern, the search can record it, and it returns a report of the shortcuts it took along with the usual BWT interval. Our motivation is pangenome graphs, where such pairs mark the places where a pattern passes through a vertex. We work out the case of a single linear reference $\Rref$, in which $β$ ranges over the length-$\ell$ windows of $\Rref$ starting at multiples of $\ell$, and $α$ over the $2^t \ell$ characters of $\Rref$ preceding such a window. We show that the resulting search counts correctly; that it crosses a stretch of the pattern matching $m$ consecutive windows of $\Rref$, whose anchors were all kept, with $O(\log m + m / 2^τ)$ shortcuts, where $2^τ\ell$ is the longest shortcut, provided the stretch and the rest of the pattern to its right occur together in the collection; and that the shortcuts can be built from the RLBWT in $O(|\Rref| (τ+ 1) \log r)$ time plus $O(\log n)$ time per BWT row they cover, plus the time to sort the anchors. On the 461-megabyte Pizza\&Chili \texttt{cere} collection of 37 genomes, shortcuts make backward search $2.3$ to $4.2$ times faster on exact patterns of length 200 to 1000, and $1.7$ to $2.0$ times faster on patterns with 1\% of their characters substituted, for 86\% more space than the RLBWT.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Near-Optimal Regret Bounds for Monotone Stochastic Optimization under Semi-Bandit Feedback
Sublinear Algorithms for Wasserstein and Total Variation Distances: Applications to Fairness and Privacy Auditing
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Resource-efficiently computing representations of probability distributions and the distances between them while only having access to the samples is a fundamental and useful problem across mathematical sciences. In this paper, we propose a generic framework to learn the probability and cumulative distribution functions (PDFs and CDFs) of a sub-Weibull, i.e. almost any light- or heavy-tailed, distribution while the samples from it arrive in a stream. The idea is to reduce these problems into estimating the frequency of an appropriately chosen subset of the support of a properly discretised distribution. We leverage this reduction to compute mergeable summaries of distributions from the stream of samples while requiring only sublinear space relative to the number of observed samples. This allows us to estimate Wasserstein and Total Variation (TV) distances between any two distributions while samples arrive in streams and from multiple sources. Our algorithms significantly improves on the existing methods for distance estimation incurring super-linear time and linear space complexities, and further extend the mergeable summaries framework to continuous distributions with possibly infinite support. Our results are tight with respect to the existing lower bounds for bounded discrete distributions. In addition, we leverage our proposed estimators of Wasserstein and TV distances to tightly audit the fairness and privacy of algorithms. We empirically demonstrate the efficiency of proposed algorithms across synthetic and real-world datasets.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Greedy Region Growing: Improved Approximations for Cutwidth, Pathwidth, Flow-Expander Decomposition, and More
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We give a new rounding technique for spreading-metric linear programs, called Greedy Region Growing, which adapts the classical technique of region growing to min-max graph layout problems and flow-expander decomposition. Using this technique, we obtain state-of-the-art approximation algorithms for several fundamental problems.
  (1) An $O(\log n)$-approximation for Cutwidth and Pathwidth, improving upon the previous bound of $O(\log n\exp(O(\sqrt{\log\log n})))$ due to Bansal, Katzelnick, and Schwartz (FOCS 2024). This matches the $Ω(\log n)$ integrality gap of the standard LP relaxations.
  (2) An $O(\log n)$-approximation for their directed analogues, Minimum Storage and Minimum Register Sufficiency on directed acyclic graphs, improving the previous bound of $O(\log^{3/2} n)$.
  (3) A $φ$-flow-expander decomposition that cuts at most an $O(φ\log n\log\log n)$ fraction of the edges. This improves the $O(φ\log n\exp(O(\sqrt{\log\log n})))$ bound of Bansal, Jambulapati, and Saranurak (ICALP 2026), and is within an $O(\log\log n)$ factor of the graph-theoretic lower bound.
  The vertex version of our algorithm also gives an $O(\log n)$-approximation for Treedepth. In particular, our results answer several open problems of Bansal, Katzelnick, and Schwartz (FOCS 2024). Technically, we also solve the conceptual question raised by their work: our technique shows how to adapt Seymour recursion to min-max objectives, and constructs $O(1)$-weak local partitions in spreading metrics.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Arboricity Matters in Triangle Counting with Random Edges
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Given a simple, unweighted, undirected graph $G=(V,E)$ with $|V|=n$ and $|E|=m$, and parameters $0 < \varepsilon, δ<1$, along with Degree, Neighbour, Pair and RandomEdge query access to $G$, we provide a query-based randomized algorithm to generate an estimate $\widehat{T}$ of the number of triangles $T$ in $G$, such that $\widehat{T} \in [(1-\varepsilon)T , (1+\varepsilon)T]$ with probability at least $1-δ$. The query complexity of our algorithm is $\widetilde{O}\left({m α\log(1/δ)}/{\varepsilon^3 T}\right)$, where $α$ is the arboricity of $G$. Our work can be seen as a natural progression to the line of recent works [Eden et al., SIAM J Comp., 2017; Assadi et al., ITCS 2019; Eden et al., SODA 2020] that considered subgraph or triangle counting with or without the use of RandomEdge query. Of these works, Eden et al. [SODA 2020] considers the role of arboricity. Our work is the first to consider how RandomEdge query can leverage the structural property of arboricity. Furthermore, continuing in the line of work of Assadi et al. [APPROX/RANDOM 2022], we also provide a lower bound of $\widetildeΩ\left({m α\log(1/δ)}/{\varepsilon^2 T}\right)$ that matches the upper bound exactly on arboricity, $δ$, and almost on $\varepsilon$.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: A Better-than-$2$ Approximation for $k$-Median Part II: Stable Instances
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We consider the $k$-median problem on general metric spaces, subject
  to the condition that the instances are $β$-stable (i.e., the
  optimal solution using $k-1$ centers has a cost at least $(1+β)$
  times that of the optimal solution with $k$ centers). We give a
  $(1.89+ε)$-approximation algorithm for such instances running in
  time $\exp(1/(β\times \mathrm{poly}(ε)))\cdot \mathrm{poly}_ε(n)$. In
  particular, for $β=\mathrm{poly}(ε)/\log n$ and $ε$ a tiny constant, this is a polynomial-time algorithm. This improves
  on previous work showing a $(2 + ε)$-approximation algorithm with
  similar running time [CGL+25]. Combined with the pseudo-approximation algorithm in our companion work, this
  results in a better-than-$2$ approximation algorithm for general $k$-median instances.
  Our main technical contribution is a novel nuanced analysis of local
  search that allows us to isolate a subset of clients on
  which we lose essentially nothing compared to the optimal solution,
  while losing an approximation factor of $3$ on the rest of the
  clients. We complement this with an algorithm based on sampling
  and partial enumeration, achieving a better-than-$2$
  approximation on the rest of the clients. Trading off these two algorithms yields our final
  approximation.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Parameterized algorithms for representing graphs as intersections of threshold graphs
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
A graph is called a threshold graph if there is an assignment of real valued weights to its vertices such that two vertices have an edge between them if and only if the sum of the weights of the two vertices is above a certain `threshold value'. We will denote the class of all threshold graphs as $TH$.
  For a graph $G=(V,E)$, if for some integer $t\geq 0$, there are $t$ many threshold graphs $\{G_i=(V,E_i)\}_{i\in [t]}$ such that we have $E=E_1\cap E_2\cap \cdots \cap E_t$, then we say that the collection of threshold graphs $\{G_i=(V,E_i)\}_{i\in [t]}$ forms a $TH$-representation of $G$ of size $t$. \emph{The intersection dimension of $G$ with respect to threshold graphs} (denoted as $dim_{TH}(G)$) is the smallest non-negative integer $t$ such that there is a $TH$-representation of $G$ of size $t$.
  It is known that for a graph $G$ and integer $t>0$, the problem of deciding whether $dim_{TH}(G)\leq t$ is NP-complete even for $t=3$. In this paper, we study this problem in the framework of parameterized algorithms. We consider the vertex cover number and the cluster vertex deletion number as our parameters. We give a FPT algorithm for determining an optimal $TH$-representation of a graph when parameterized by its vertex cover number. Our main result is an efficient parameterized approximation scheme for this problem when parameterized by the cluster vertex deletion number of $G$.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: LOCAL LLL in $\operatorname{poly}(\log\log n)$ Rounds
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We provide a $\operatorname{poly}(\log\log n)$-round randomized LOCAL algorithm for the constructive Lovász Local Lemma with polynomial criterion $pd^{c} < 1$, for a sufficiently large constant $c$. The best previous general round complexity was $\widetilde O(\log n)$. The key ingredient is a local reduction that amplifies the LLL probability exponent quadratically, while increasing the dependency radius only by a constant factor.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Can Rényi Accountants Beat Lossless Accountants for DP-SGD?
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Recent frameworks in differential privacy (DP), such as privacy loss distributions and $f$-DP, provide lossless representations of the privacy leakage of mechanisms. These approaches are often considered to yield tighter $(\varepsilon, δ)$-DP guarantees than those obtained from relaxed notions such as Rényi DP. But is that always the case? We study this question for differentially private stochastic gradient descent (DP-SGD) with fixed-size batches under replace adjacency. Our key observation is that in this setting, privacy accounting based on Rényi DP can use a pair of worst-case distributions (i.e., a dominating pair) that differs from the one used in the lossless frameworks. In particular, we characterize the worst-case distributions as two-dimensional Gaussian mixtures and derive an improved Rényi DP bound for DP-SGD. Numerical and asymptotic comparisons show that across various hyperparameter settings, a Rényi DP accountant based on the new bound can yield better privacy guarantees than those obtained from the lossless frameworks.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Non-Exclusive Notifications for Ride-Hailing at Lyft I: Single-Cycle Approximation Algorithms
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
Ride-hailing platforms increasingly rely on non-exclusive notifications--broadcasting a single request to multiple drivers simultaneously--to mitigate inefficiencies caused by uncertain driver acceptance. In this paper, the first in a two-part collaboration with Lyft, we formally model the Notification Set Selection Problem for a single decision cycle, where the platform determines the optimal subset of drivers to notify for each incoming ride request. We analyze this combinatorial optimization problem under two contention-resolution protocols: First Acceptance (FA), which prioritizes speed by assigning the ride to the first responder, and Best Acceptance (BA), which prioritizes match quality by selecting the highest-valued accepting driver.
  We show that welfare maximization under both mechanisms is NP-hard, ruling out a polynomial-time exact algorithm unless P=NP. Despite this hardness, we establish several positive algorithmic results. For FA, we develop a Polynomial Time Approximation Scheme (PTAS) for the single-rider problem. For the general matching setting, we provide a (1-1/e)-approximation algorithm that applies to both FA and BA. Along the way, we show that the FA valuation function constitutes a novel discrete choice model with structural properties of independent interest. For BA, we further prove that the welfare objective is monotone and submodular and exploit additional structure to obtain an approximation guarantee that surpasses the classical (1-1/e) barrier. Finally, when acceptance probabilities are independent of the drivers, we show that the BA problem can be solved exactly in polynomial time through a linear programming formulation. We evaluate our algorithms on synthetic instances and on instances calibrated using real ride-sharing data from Lyft, demonstrating strong empirical performance.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Prophet Inequalities with Cancellation Costs
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
Most of the literature on online algorithms and sequential decision-making in revenue management focuses on settings with irrevocable decisions. Motivated by modern applications such as cloud spot markets, selling banner ads, and online hotel booking, we study "prophet inequalities with cancellations" under linear cancellation costs (the buyback model). A sequence of independent random variables $X_1, X_2, \ldots$ with known distributions is revealed one by one. After accepting $X_j$, a decision-maker may later discard it and accept another variable at a cost of $f \times X_j$, where $f \ge 0$. The goal is to maximize the expected net reward: the value of the final accepted variable minus the total cancellation cost. We compare online policies with an omniscient optimal offline "prophet" benchmark.
  Our first main result is an optimal prophet inequality for all parameters $f \ge 0$. We fully characterize the worst-case competitive ratio of the optimal online policy against the optimal offline benchmark via a differential equation, for which we provide a constructive solution. Our second main result is a simple polynomial-time randomized adaptive policy that achieves this optimal competitive ratio. Our policy is order-agnostic (in the sense of Samuel-Cahn (1984)): it only needs to know the set of distributions and not their arrival order. These results follow from reductions to a continuous "generalized flow problem," viewed as the dual to a factor-revealing LP for the worst-case competitive ratio. Our techniques include a geometric interpretation of its solution via a differential equation and the embedding of random variables into specific Poisson point processes. We also use these building blocks to construct lower-bound instances and to design and analyze our

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Scrambled Linear Pseudorandom Number Generators
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: $\mathbf F_2$-linear pseudorandom number generators are very popular due to their high speed, to the ease with which generators with a sizable state space can be created, and to their provable theoretical properties. However, they suffer from linear artifacts that show as failures in linearity-related statistical tests such as the binary-rank and the linear-complexity test. In this paper, we give two new contributions. First, we introduce two new $\mathbf F_2$-linear transformations that have been handcrafted to have good statistical properties and at the same time to be programmable very efficiently on superscalar processors, or even directly in hardware. Then, we describe some scramblers, that is, nonlinear functions applied to the state array that reduce or delete the linear artifacts, and propose combinations of linear transformations and scramblers that give extremely fast pseudorandom number generators of high quality. A novelty in our approach is that we use ideas from the theory of filtered linear-feedback shift registers to prove some properties of our scramblers, rather than relying purely on heuristics. In the end, we provide simple, extremely fast generators that use a few hundred bits of memory, have provable properties, and pass strong statistical tests.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Exponential Local Search in Bounded-Occurrence MAX-CSP
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We study the number of improving steps that local search may require for $(2,2,r)$-MCA (Maximum Constraint Assignment), a bounded-occurrence version of MAX-CSP with valued constraints in which every constraint involves at most two variables, every variable occurs in at most two constraints, and every variable takes one of $r$ values. We consider the flip neighborhood, where two assignments are neighbors if they differ in the value of exactly one variable; moving to such a neighbor is called a flip. Local search repeatedly performs improving flips, that is, flips that strictly increase the objective value, until a local optimum is reached.
  Our main result is that $(2,2,5)$-MCA has the all-exp property: there is an infinite family of instances with initial assignments for which every sequence of improving flips ending in a local optimum has length exponential in the number of variables. Thus, on these instances, local search requires exponentially many steps regardless of which improving flip is chosen at each step. This is the first all-exp result for $(2,2,r)$-MCA for any value of $r$, and our result extends to every $r\ge 5$.
  In contrast, for $(2,2,2)$-MCA every sequence of improving flips has length at most quadratic in the number of variables~\cite{Kaz2020,KCJ2020}. We give a short, direct proof of this result.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Approximation Algorithms for Graphic Multi-Depot TSP and Graphic Multi-Path TSP
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We give improved approximation algorithms for two graphic TSP variants. First, we consider Multi-Depot TSP on graphic instances. In this variant, we are given an undirected graph with a set of depot vertices, and we are tasked with finding an Eulerian multi-edge set that connects each non-depot vertex to at least one depot. For this problem, Deppert, Kaul and Mnich (ESA 2023) presented a 3/2-approximation algorithm with running time exponential in the number of depots. We improve this result to a fully polynomial 3/2-approximation. Our algorithm is a variant of the classic Christofides-Serdyukov algorithm with an improved and simple analysis. On subcubic instances, we improve the approximation guarantee to 4/3 using the technique of removable pairings introduced by Mömke and Svensson (J. ACM 2016). We use a removable pairing to construct a set of disjoint cycles that can be completed to a cheap feasible solution. Second, we consider the Graphic Multi-Path TSP, which was previously considered by Alimi, Dahlmeier, Mömke, Pabst and Vargas Koch (SOSA 2026) who give a 2-approximation for this problem. Additionally, the authors present a reduction that shows that any better-than-two approximation for Graphic Multi-Depot TSP immediately leads to an improvement for Graphic Multi-Path TSP. We give an improved algorithm and analysis that yield an approximation guarantee of 1.9304.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Tractability of Hard Digraph Cut Problems on Eulerian Instances: Treewidth Reduction and Reducing CMSO to Unbreakable Eulerian Instances
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
Eulerian digraphs retain the directional structure of general digraphs while exhibiting a symmetry of cuts reminiscent of undirected graphs. We show that this symmetry extends beyond individual cuts to two fundamental techniques in parameterized algorithms for undirected cut problems: treewidth reduction and recursive understanding and randomized contractions. Both of these techniques have proved useful for dealing with undirected graph cut problems as each of them reduces the problem at hand on general undirected instances to ones that have bounded treewidth or that are highly connected, respectively.
  In this work we prove an edge-cut analogue of the treewidth-reduction theorem of Marx, O'Sullivan, and Razgon [ACM TALG 2013], and an Eulerian analogue of the reduction of CMSO model checking to unbreakable instances due to Lokshtanov, Ramanujan, Saurabh, and Zehavi [ICALP 2018]. Both these results allow us to reduce several problems on general Eulerian digraphs to Eulerian digraphs whose underlying undirected graph has bounded treewidth, or to Eulerian instances that are highly connected, thus bringing to Eulerian digraphs two fundamental tools from the undirected parameterized cut toolkit for which no counterparts are known on arbitrary digraphs.
  Beyond their structural significance, these results have substantial algorithmic consequences: they yield FPT algorithms for several directed cut problems that are W[1]-hard in general. We show that Directed Multicut and Directed Edge Odd Cycle Transversal are FPT on Eulerian digraphs when parameterized by the solution size and the number of terminal pairs, and just the solution size, respectively. This is in sharp contrast to general digraphs, where the first problem is W[1]-hard even for 4 terminal pairs, and the second is W[1]-hard in general. We also obtain FPT algorithms for Directed Edge Multiway Cut-Uncut and Directed Steiner Cut.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Subset Sum and Integer Programming Feasibility Test in Near-Optimal Time
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We give an $O_{d,\varepsilon}(n+N^{d+\varepsilon})$-time algorithm for multidimensional subset sum on an explicitly listed multiset of $n$ vectors in $[-N,N]^d$, for every fixed $d$ and $\varepsilon>0$. This directly implies an $O_{d,\varepsilon}(n+N^{d+\varepsilon})$-time algorithm for feasibility test of integer programming. Prior to our work, the best-known algorithm has a running time of $O_{d}(n+N^{O(d^2)})$ [Eisenbrand, Weismantel'19]. Specifically, if $d=1$, our algorithm runs in $O_{\varepsilon}(n+N^{1+\varepsilon})$-time for the standard subset sum problem, which is near-linear in the largest input integer. Prior to our work, subset sum can be solved in time near-linear in the target $t$ [Bringmann'17], or near-linear in the mixed parameter $\sqrt{Nt}$ [Chen, Lian, Mao, Zhang'24]. It is a fundamental open problem whether the algorithm can be made near-linear in $N$, which is settled affirmatively in this paper up to an arbitrary small $N^{\varepsilon}$ term.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: The Communication Complexity of the Coin Problem
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We study the two-player communication complexity of the \textsf{Coin} problem. Here, two players, denoted Alice and Bob, are given up to $n$ individual i.i.d. random coins, and asked to output whether there are more heads or tails. An immediate approach is for Alice to send Bob her exact numbers of heads and tails, yielding a deterministic protocol with one-way communication cost $O(\log n)$ bits. Indeed, this is provably optimal in the related multi-player and streaming settings [Braverman, Garg, Woodruff, FOCS'20].
  Our contribution is to show that this is not the right answer in the one-way two-player setting. Instead, we prove a $Ω(\log\log n)$ bit lower bound for the constant error-rate regime, and a $Ω(\log(1/δ))$ bit lower bound for arbitrarily small error rates, $δ\geq n^{-0.1}$. We also complement these with a tight one-way protocol using $O(\log\log n + \log(1/δ))$ bits of communication. Unlike the previous works, our lower bounds avoid intricate direct information-theoretic arguments. Instead, our $Ω(\log(1/δ))$ bound is via a standard fooling-set style argument, whilst our $Ω(\log\log n)$ bound is via a novel yet simple reduction from the \textsf{Gap-Greater-Than} problem. This reduction is our main technical contribution, and can be seen as loosely inspired by the \emph{Robust Communication Complexity} arguments of [Chakrabarti, Cormode, McGregor, STOC'08].
  Finally, we also show that our constant-error lower bound and protocol can be adapted to the multi-round setting: up to polynomial factors in $r$, the $r$-round communication complexity of the coin problem is $Θ\left((\log\log n)^{1/r}\right)$ bits.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Move-rb: Faster Bi-Directional r-indexes and Approximate Pattern Matching
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Approximate pattern matching (APM) on highly repetitive texts is a central task in bioinformatics. Bi-directional r-indexes support left- and right-extension of a pattern and thereby accelerate APM algorithms based on search schemes, but existing variants -- br-index and b-move -- suffer from two bottlenecks: $O(σ)$ character-predecessor/-successor queries on the run-length-encoded BWT per extension, and predecessor queries on sparse bit vectors to maintain a value in the suffix array interval and to access the PLCP array while locating. We present Move-rb, a bi-directional r-index built on the optimized r-index Move-r. Although Move-rb is 2x larger than br-index, it is up to 24% smaller than b-move, answers APM queries 1-4 orders of magnitude faster than br-index, 1.9-10x faster than b-move and up to 5.5x faster than the state-of-the-art bi-directional (uncompressed) FM-index columba, which is 36-42x larger. Memory usage (including index size) during APM locate queries is reduced by 1.5x (up to 6.5x) for Hamming distance and 2.5x (up to 7.4x) for edit distance. Move-rb can be constructed 3-14x faster while using 19-141x less memory than br-index, b-move and columba. A variant using a relative Lempel-Ziv-encoded suffix array locates up to 10x faster while being 1.2-2.4x larger. We achieve these speedups by optimizing index operations and search scheme APM algorithms: Without a direction switch, Move-rb computes an all-$k$-character extension in output-optimal $O(k)$ time and a single-character extension in the same time. Augmenting Move-rb with $O((r+\overleftarrow{r})\log(n/r_{\min})\logσ)$ bits reduces a single-character extension to $O(\logσ)$ time, where $r$ and $\overleftarrow{r}$ are the numbers of runs in the BWT of the text and its reverse, and $r_{\min}=\min(r,\overleftarrow{r})$. A direction switch incurs only $O(\log\log_ω(n/r_{\min}))$ additional time.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: On the (In)Approximability of the Monitoring Edge Geodetic Set Problem
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
The minimum \emph{Monitoring Edge-Geodetic Set} problem asks for a minimum vertex subset $M$ such that for every edge $e$ of the input graph $G$, there exist a two vertices $u,v \in M$, that monitor $e$, i.e. every shortest path between $u$ and $v$ in $G$ contains $e$.
  We prove that this problem cannot be approximated within an $Ω(\log n)$ ratio in polynomial time unless $\mathsf{NP} \subseteq \mathsf{ZTIME}(n^{O(\log \log n)})$. Additionally, we establish hardness and conditional running-time lower bounds for exact algorithms on $2$-degenerate, $3$-degenerate, and $1$-apex $2$-degenerate graphs.
  Moreover, we design an approximation algorithm for hereditary graph classes with efficiently computable, truly sublinear-size balanced separators. This achieves an $O(n^{\frac{1}{4}} \sqrt{\log n})$ approximation ratio for $K_h$-minor-free graphs ($h=O(1)$), bounded genus graphs, and $k$-apex graphs ($k=O(n^{\frac{1}{4}})$). For graphs with bounded treewidth, the algorithm yields an $O(\log^{3/2} n)$ approximation ratio.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Tight Approximations for Fixed-Order Vehicle Routing with Stochastic Demands
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We study the vehicle routing problem (VRP) with stochastic demands, where each client has an independent demand with a known distribution, and its realized demand is observed only on the first visit. We consider a priori and restocking policies that fix the client order before observing demands and serve each client's entire demand before first visiting the next. Gupta, Nagarajan, and Ravi (Oper. Res., 2012) developed randomized a priori $(α+1)$-approximation and $(α+2)$-approximation algorithms for splittable and unsplittable deliveries, respectively, where $α$ is the approximation ratio of a metric traveling salesman problem (TSP) algorithm. We improve these approximation ratios to $2$ and $3$ by using their replenishment rules with a TSP tour constructed via matroid parity. We also obtain deterministic a priori $(2+\varepsilon)$-approximation and $(3+\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithms by compressing the distributions of cumulative demands to select an initial stock in polynomial time. All guarantees are relative to the general adaptive optimum. We then establish matching lower bounds of $2$ and $3$ that hold even for the more general class of randomized restocking policies. Finally, we apply our matroid-parity construction to improve approximation ratios for several VRP variants with deterministic demands.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Improved Massively Parallel Shortest Path Computation
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We present new algorithms for approximate shortest path computation in weighted undirected graphs within the Massively Parallel Computation (MPC) model. Specifically, we construct an $a$-approximate Single-Source Shortest Path (SSSP) oracle: Given a query consisting of a source vertex $u \in V$, the oracle returns $a$-approximate distances $δ(u,v)$ for all $v \in V$.
  Fix an $n$-vertex weighted undirected graph. We consider two regimes of the MPC model: the near-linear regime, where each machine has $\tildeΘ(n)$ memory, and the heterogeneous regime, where all machines have $Θ(n^γ)$ memory for some constant $γ\in (0,1]$, except for a single machine with $\tildeΘ(n)$ memory. We develop randomised algorithms that construct $O(1)$-approximate SSSP oracles in $O(\log\log n)$ rounds in the near-linear regime and in $O(\log^2\log n)$ rounds in the heterogeneous regime. These oracles answer distance queries in $O(1)$ rounds. Our results improve upon the recent work of Dory and Matar (SPAA 2024) which, for the same total memory, requires $\left(\log\log n\right)^{2+O(1/γ)}$ rounds and applies only to unweighted graphs in the heterogeneous setting.
  We say that $\tilde N_k(u)$ is the approximate $k$-nearest neighbourhood of a vertex $u$ if there exists an approximate distance estimate $δ$ such that $\tilde N_k(u)$ consists of the $k$ vertices closest to $u$ according to $δ$, breaking ties by vertex ID. The main technical ingredient is a new method for efficiently computing approximate $n^{O(γ)}$-nearest neighbourhoods in the heterogeneous MPC model in $O(\log^2\log n)$ rounds.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: A Deterministic $0.401$-Approximation for Non-monotone Submodular Maximization under Matroid Constraints
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
Submodular maximization arises in a wide range of combinatorial optimization problems and has been extensively studied from the perspective of approximation algorithms. For maximizing nonnegative, non-monotone submodular functions subject to a matroid constraint, randomized algorithms achieve a $0.401$-approximation, whereas obtaining comparable deterministic guarantees remains challenging. In this paper, we present a deterministic $0.401$-approximation algorithm in the exact value and independence oracle model, improving upon the previous deterministic guarantee of $(0.385-\varepsilon)$ \cite{ChenGLSZ2026}.
  Our algorithm builds on the extended multilinear extension and provides a deterministic implementation of the recursive guided framework underlying the randomized $0.401$-approximation algorithm. The main technical ingredient is a direction oracle supported on at most two partitioned matroid bases. This oracle simultaneously satisfies the growth condition required by the extended-multilinear update and an approximate stationarity condition needed to construct the recursive guides. The resulting finite-support representation enables exact evaluation of the relevant expectations and marginal values without random sampling. The algorithm uses polynomially many value- and independence-oracle queries.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Highway Dimension: a Metric View
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
Realistic metric spaces (such as road/transportation networks) tend to be much more algorithmically tractable than general metrics. In an attempt to formalize this intuition, Abraham et al. (SODA 2010, JACM 2016) introduced the notion of highway dimension. A weighted graph $G$ has highway dimension $h$ if for every ball $B$ of radius $\approx4r$, there is a hitting set of size $h$ hitting all the shortest paths of length $>r$ in $B$. Unfortunately, this definition fails to incorporate some very natural metric spaces such as the grid graph, and the Euclidean plane.
  We relax the definition of highway dimension by demanding to hit only approximate shortest paths. In addition to generalizing the original definition, this new definition also incorporates all doubling spaces (in particular the grid graph and the Euclidean plane). We then construct a PTAS for TSP under this new definition (improving a QPTAS w.r.t. the original more restrictive definition of Feldmann et al. (SICOMP 2018)). Finally, we develop a basic metric toolkit for spaces with small highway dimension by constructing padded decompositions, sparse covers/partitions, and tree covers. An abundance of applications follow.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 57 pages. This is the TheoretiCS journal version

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: The Online Steinitz Problem
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Inspired by Steinitz's celebrated result (1913) and recent online vector-balancing results of Kulkarni et al. (2024) and Aden-Ali (2026), we introduce the online Steinitz problem: $T$ vectors in $\mathbb R^d$, each of $\ell_2$-norm at most $1$ and with total sum zero, arrive one at a time and must be assigned immediately and irrevocably to unused positions of an array. The goal is to keep every prefix sum of the resulting order small. We first obtain deterministic prefix-discrepancy bounds of $O(\log T)$ for $d=1$ and $O(\sqrt T)$ for $d\ge2$. Our main contribution is a general reduction that converts deterministic and randomized online vector-balancing algorithms, which assign signs to arriving vectors, into online ordering algorithms. Combined with recent vector-balancing results, this yields a randomized algorithm with prefix discrepancy $O(\log T+\sqrt{d\log T})$ and running time $O(dT\log T)$. The guarantee holds with high probability against an oblivious adversary. The reduction also gives bounds for sparse vectors and extends to inputs in arbitrary compact convex bodies. Finally, we prove matching lower bounds in both the deterministic and randomized cases.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Averaged Annealed Markov Chains Achieve the Algorithmic Threshold for Tensor PCA, Part I: Glauber Dynamics
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: In the tensor principal components analysis (tensor PCA) problem, we are asked to recover an unknown vector in $\{\pm1\}^N$ from a noisy observation of its $k$-th tensor power, for a fixed $k\ge3$. Tensor PCA exhibits a well-studied information-computation gap: global algorithms such as spectral methods and sum-of-squares work above an algorithmic threshold, below which we know matching lower bounds (against these and some other restricted models of computation). In contrast, local algorithms such as Markov chains were only known to succeed from a random initialization at a polynomially larger signal-to-noise ratio, and were believed to be inferior to global algorithms for tensor PCA. We show that Glauber dynamics, when supplemented with annealing and ergodic averaging, achieves polynomial-time strong recovery above the algorithmic threshold from a uniformly random initialization, demonstrating that local Markov chains can succeed all the way down to the algorithmic threshold from an uninformative cold start.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Graph Matching in Random Geometric Graphs I: Efficient Algorithms
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We study the recovery of the hidden vertex correspondence between two correlated dense random geometric graphs. Each graph is generated from $n$ latent unit vectors in $\mathbb R^d$; the vectors $u_i^A$ and $u_i^B$ of corresponding vertices satisfy $\langle u_i^A,u_i^B\rangle=ρ$, and the vertex labels of the second graph are permuted by an unknown permutation $π$. For every fixed correlation $ρ\in(0,1]$ and every edge density bounded away from zero and one, we give a randomized polynomial time algorithm that recovers $π$ exactly with probability tending to one whenever $d\ge(\log n)^L$, where $L$ depends only on the correlation and the density bounds. The algorithm assigns to each vertex a signature formed by counting decorated paths with a constant number of seeds. The number of such seeded templates grows exponentially with the path length, with an arbitrarily large constant base, so the resulting statistics amplify an arbitrarily small constant correlation. We control the dependencies created by the latent geometry in two ways: when $d$ is larger than $n/(\log n)^{L_0}$ for a suitable constant $L_0$, by comparing local moments with those of correlated Erdős--Rényi graphs; for smaller $d$, by spectral estimation of the latent geometry combined with a harmonic correction. We also provide low-degree evidence for a tradeoff between the correlation and the computational cost.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: On Estimating Degree Distribution in Streaming and Query Models
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
Given a graph $G=(V,E)$ with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, let $C(d)=|\{v\in V:°(v)\ge d\}|$ denote its complementary cumulative degree histogram (CCDH), and let $h$ be the $h$-index of $G$. The goal is to compute a $(\varepsilon_D,\varepsilon_R)$-bi-criteria multiplicative approximation of $C$, where $\varepsilon_D$ and $\varepsilon_R$ control the approximation in the domain and range, respectively. In this work, we study the complexity of this problem in the streaming model and an augmented query model that provides access to uniformly random edge queries in addition to standard local queries.
  We design a model-agnostic algorithm that combines uniformly sampled vertices and edges to estimate the CCDH. Ignoring the dependence on the approximation parameters and polylogarithmic factors in $n$, the complexity in the streaming model is $Θ(m/h)$: the upper bound holds for a single-pass algorithm, while the lower bound holds even for multi-pass algorithms. In the query model, the complexity is $Θ(m/h)$ for adaptive algorithms. For non-adaptive algorithms, we give an upper bound of $O(n/h+m/h)$ and establish lower bounds through a reduction from estimating the number of distinct elements in a multiset when sampling without replacement.
  Our results resolve an open problem in sublinear graph algorithms posed in Sublinear.info (Problem 98). Finally, we validate our algorithm through extensive empirical evaluations on real-world graphs.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Improved Bounds for Estimating Average Degree of Graphs
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We propose a randomized parameter-oblivious algorithm that, given query access to a graph $G$ with arboricity $α$, and average degree $d$, makes $\widetilde{O}\left(\fracα{\varepsilon^2d}\right)$ Degree and $\widetilde{O}\left(\frac{1}{\varepsilon^2}\right)$ RandEdge queries to obtain an estimate $\widehat{d}$ satisfying $\widehat{d} \in (1\pm\varepsilon)d$. This also yields an algorithm that uses $\widetilde{O}\left(\frac{1}{\varepsilon^2}\min(d,\fracα{d})\right)$ Degree and RandEdge queries. This improves the $\widetilde{O}_{\varepsilon,\log n}(\frac{1}{\varepsilon^2}$ $\min(d,\sqrt{\frac{n}{d}}))$ query algorithm of [Beretta et al., SODA 2026] that has access to Degree, Neighbour, and RandEdge queries.
  We show that any algorithm that has access to Degree, Neighbour, and RandEdge queries, must make at least $Ω\left(\min\left(d,\fracα{d}\right)\right)$ queries, even with the knowledge of $n$ and $α$. Even with Pair and FullNbr queries, an algorithm must make $Ω\left(\min\left(d,\fracα{d}\right)\right)$ queries for certain ranges of $α$. When $n$ is unknown, any algorithm with access to all the queries discussed above must make $Ω\left(\min\left(d,\fracα{d}\right)\right)$ queries.
  We also establish that any sublinear algorithm using Degree and RandEdge queries must make at least $Ω(\frac{1}{\varepsilon})$ RandEdge queries. Furthermore, any algorithm having access to Degree, FullNbr, and RandEdge queries that makes $o(\frac{1}{\varepsilon^2})$ RandEdge queries must make $Ω(\fracα{\varepsilon^2d})$ Degree and FullNbr queries. This settles the query complexity of estimating average degree using Degree and FullNbr queries.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Dynamic Maximal Independent Set using Predictions
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We present the first dynamic maximal independent set (MIS) of a graph with $n$ vertices and up to $m$ edges under edge updates in the prediction model, where a predicted update sequence is available for offline preprocessing before the real updates arrive online. We consider the incremental (insertion-only), decremental (deletions-only), and fully dynamic (insertions and deletions) models. Without predictions, deterministic algorithms need worst-case update time of $O(n)$ for decremental and $O(m)$ for incremental and fully dynamic settings. Bernstein et al.~[SODA26] proved under the combinatorial BMM conjecture, combinatorial incremental algorithms against an adaptive adversary require $Ω(n^{1-o(1)})$ amortized update time.
  We present deterministic incremental, decremental, and fully dynamic algorithms whose update times depend on the prediction error. This error is measured by the number $η_e$ of mispredicted updates, and by the number $η_v$ and total degree $η_v^*$ of vertices whose MIS membership was mispredicted. With $O(mn)$ preprocessing, our decremental and incremental algorithms achieve worst-case update times $O(η_v)$ and $O(η_e+η_v^*)$, respectively. Our fully dynamic algorithm achieves $O(η_e+η_v^*)$ worst-case update time with $O(un)$ preprocessing for $u$ updates. We also give space-efficient variants using $O(m)$ space for the decremental and $O(m\sqrt{m})$ for the incremental setting, at the cost of a logarithmic overhead in worst-case update time.
  Our algorithms satisfy consistency, robustness, and smooth degradation, the required properties of algorithms with predictions. They can also utilize the general error correction framework of Khan et al.~[Arxiv26], relaxing the error measures from first point of difference to prefix matching (for partially dynamic) and set edit distance (for fully dynamic), maintaining the same bounds.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Distributed $(Δ+1)$-Coloring in $O(\sqrtΔ+\log^* n)$ Rounds
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We give a deterministic distributed algorithm for $(Δ+1)$-coloring an $n$-node graph of maximum degree $Δ$ in $O(\sqrtΔ+\log^* n)$ rounds in both the LOCAL and CONGEST models. More generally, $(°+1)$-list coloring with lists from a color space of size $C\geqΔ+1$ can be solved in $O(\sqrtΔ\log(1+C/Δ)+\log^* n)$ rounds; in CONGEST, we assume $C\leq n^{O(1)}$. The algorithm combines Barenboim's polynomial coloring procedure with arbdefective decompositions, degree reduction, and a short family of hash functions. Using the polynomial procedure in the degree-reduction framework already gives an $O(\sqrtΔ\logΔ+\log^* n)$-round algorithm when $C=O(Δ)$. Hashing adapts the color space to the current degree and removes the logarithmic factor. We prove the existence of the hash family by the probabilistic method and compute it by deterministic exhaustive search, using unrestricted local computation. We also give an explicit variant based on lossless expanders that avoids this search and achieves $O(\sqrtΔ+\log^* n)$ rounds for $C=O(Δ)$.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Near-Linear Time Computation of Welzl Orders on Graphs with Linear Neighborhood Complexity
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
Orders with low crossing number, introduced by Welzl, are a fundamental tool in range searching and computational geometry. Recently, they have found important applications in structural graph theory: set systems with linear shatter functions correspond to graph classes with linear neighborhood complexity. For such set systems S = (U, F), Welzl's theorem guarantees the existence of orders with only O(log^2 n) crossings, n = |U|. A series of works has progressively improved the runtime for computing such orders, from Chazelle and Welzl's original O(|U|^3 |F|) bound (Chazelle and Welzl, 1989), through Har-Peled's O(|U|^2|F|) (Har-Peled, 2009), to the recent sampling-based methods of Csikós and Mustafa (Csikós and Mustafa, 2024).
  We present a randomized algorithm that computes Welzl orders for set systems with linear primal and dual shatter functions in expected time O(||S|| log ||S||), where ||S|| = |U| + sum_{X in F} |X| is the size of the canonical input representation. The algorithm achieves an asymptotically optimal O(log n) crossing bound. As an application, we compute compact neighborhood covers in graph classes with (near-)linear neighborhood complexity in time O((n+m) log n), where n and m are the numbers of vertices and edges. Our result also improves the runtime of first-order model checking on monadically stable graph classes from O(n^(5+epsilon)) to O(n^(3+epsilon)).

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Graph determination problem from knowledge of its subgraphs
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: In the context of graph reconstruction studies, this paper addresses the problem defined as follows: given a sample of vertex-coloured graphs, each associated with a number, does there exist a connected graph containing exactly the given number of induced subgraphs isomorphic to each graph in the sample, such that every edge of the solution graph is included in at least one of these subgraphs. This paper first shows that this problem is $Σ$______-complete. The associated optimisation problem is to determine the minimum number of vertices in a solution graph, if one exists. For instances consisting of two paths, we prove NP-completeness in general and give a polynomial-time dynamic programming algorithm when one path is monochromatic.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Online Tree Caching
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We initiate the study of a natural and practically relevant new variant of online caching where the to-be-cached items can have dependencies. We assume that the universe is a tree $T$ and items are tree nodes; we require that if a node $v$ is cached then the whole subtree $T(v)$ rooted at $v$ is cached as well. This theoretical problem finds an immediate application in the context of forwarding table optimization in IP routing and software-defined networks.
  We present an elegant online deterministic algorithm TC for this problem, and rigorously prove that its competitive ratio is $O(\mathrm{height}(T) \cdot k_{\mathrm{ONL}}/(k_{\mathrm{ONL}}-k_{\mathrm{OPT}}+1))$, where $k_{\mathrm{ONL}}$ and $k_{\mathrm{OPT}}$ denote the cache sizes of an online and the optimal offline algorithm, respectively. The result is optimal up to a factor of $O(\mathrm{height}(T))$. We complement the theoretical analysis with an empirical study on synthetic workloads and CAIDA backbone traffic, illustrating the trade-off between hit rate and cache-update cost.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: Journal version of the SPAA 2017 paper, extended with an empirical evaluation

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Faster Sublinear Maximal Independent Set Size
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We give a sublinear-time algorithm for estimating the size of a maximal independent set in a graph using adjacency-query access with expected running time $\tilde{O}(n^{1+1/3})$, improving over the previous $\tilde{O}(n^{1+1/2})$ bound of Mahadabi et al. [MRTV26]. As a consequence of a reduction of [MRTV26], this also improves the running time for sublinear metric Steiner forest. We further show that a bi-criteria estimate of the $k$-center objective in general metrics can be obtained via a reduction to maximal independent set size estimation.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Elfs, transducers and quantum walks
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Electric flow sampling (elfs) is a new tool in the quantum walk toolbox and a useful primitive for solving search, sampling and optimization problems on graphs. We refine this tool by showing that there exists a zero-error transducer for implementing elfs. More broadly, we establish a zero-error transducer for reflecting about the intersection of two subspaces, yielding an errorfree transducer version of the effective gap lemma. Building on this result, we obtain improved quantum walk algorithms for estimating effective resistances and span program witness sizes with an optimal error scaling, and for sampling from the random walk arrival distribution, via the composition of many elfs. Using this last algorithm, we obtain an up-to-quadratic quantum speedup for semi-supervised learning on expander graphs.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Ramsey Meets Simultaneous Planarity: Vertex Integrity and Pathwidth
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We study the following simultaneous embedding problem: Given k graphs on the same vertex set with the same pairwise intersection, do they admit planar drawings that coincide on their shared graph? We establish fixed-parameter tractability with respect to the vertex integrity of the union graph (that is, the union of the input graphs) plus k, resolving an open question and generalizing the known algorithm parameterized by vertex cover number plus k. Our main technical contribution on the way towards this result is the extension of the recently introduced Ramsey pruning technique beyond ordering problems. Finally, we complement our tractability result with a lower bound that establishes NP-hardness when both k and the pathwidth of the union graph are bounded by constants, ruling out a generalization of our main result to path- or treewidth.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Hardness, Tractability and Density Thresholds of finite Pinwheel Scheduling Variants
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
The k-Visits problem is a recently introduced finite version of Pinwheel Scheduling [Kanellopoulos et al., SODA 2026]. Given the deadlines of n tasks, the problem asks whether there exists a schedule of length kn executing each task exactly k times, with no deadline expiring between consecutive visits (executions) of each task.
  In this work we prove that 2-Visits is strongly NP-complete even when the maximum multiplicity of the input is equal to 2, settling an open question from [Kanellopoulos et al., SODA 2026] and contrasting the tractability of 2-Visits for simple sets. On the other hand, we prove that 2-Visits is in RP when the number of distinct deadlines is constant, thus making progress on another open question regarding the parameterization of 2-Visits by the number of numbers. We then generalize all existing positive results for 2-Visits to a version of the problem where some tasks must be visited once and some other tasks twice, while providing evidence that some of these results are unlikely to transfer to 3-Visits.
  Lastly, we establish bounds for the density thresholds of k-Visits, analogous to the $(5/6)$-threshold of Pinwheel Scheduling [Kawamura, STOC 2024]; in particular, we show a $\sqrt{2}-1/2\approx 0.9142$ lower bound for the density threshold of 2-Visits and prove that the density threshold of k-Visits approaches $5/6\approx 0.8333$ for $k \to \infty$.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Speed-Oblivious Online Scheduling: Knowing (Precise) Speeds is not Necessary
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We consider online scheduling on unrelated (heterogeneous) machines in a speed-oblivious setting, where an algorithm is unaware of the exact job-dependent processing speeds. We show strong impossibility results for clairvoyant and non-clairvoyant algorithms and overcome them in models inspired by practical settings: (i) we provide competitive learning-augmented algorithms, assuming that (possibly erroneous) predictions on the speeds are given, and (ii) we provide competitive algorithms for the speed-ordered model, where a single global order of machines according to their unknown job-dependent speeds is known. We prove strong theoretical guarantees and evaluate our findings on a representative heterogeneous multi-core processor. These seem to be the first empirical results for scheduling algorithms with predictions that are evaluated in a non-synthetic hardware environment.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Broadcasting under Structural Restrictions
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
In the Telephone Broadcast problem we are given a graph $G=(V,E)$ with a designated source vertex $s\in V$. Our goal is to transmit a message, which is initially known only to $s$, to all vertices of the graph by using a process where in each round an informed vertex may transmit the message to one of its uninformed neighbors. The optimization objective is to minimize the number of rounds.
  Following up on several recent works, we investigate the structurally parameterized complexity of Telephone Broadcast. In particular, we first strengthen existing NP-hardness results by showing that the problem remains NP-complete on graphs of bounded tree-depth and also on cactus graphs which are one vertex deletion away from being path forests. Motivated by this (severe) hardness, we study several other parameterizations of the problem and obtain FPT algorithms parameterized by vertex integrity (generalizing a recent FPT algorithm parameterized by vertex cover by Fomin, Fraigniaud, and Golovach [TCS 2024]) and by distance to clique, as well as FPT approximation algorithms parameterized by clique-cover and cluster vertex deletion. Furthermore, we obtain structural results that relate the length of the optimal broadcast protocol of a graph $G$ with its pathwidth and tree-depth. By presenting a substantial improvement over the best previously known bound for pathwidth (Aminian, Kamali, Seyed-Javadi, and Sumedha [ICALP 2025]) we exponentially improve the approximation ratio achievable in polynomial time on graphs of bounded pathwidth from $\mathcal{O}(4^\mathrm{pw})$ to $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{pw})$.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Fast Quantized Johnson$-$Lindenstrauss Transforms
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
Quantization has emerged as one of the primary techniques for reducing the memory footprint of large language models during inference. A prominent example is Quantized Johnson$-$Lindenstrauss (QJL), which compresses KV caches using 1-bit asymmetric quantization while approximately preserving the inner products required by the attention mechanism. Recent theoretical and practical work aims at replacing the dense Gaussian projections used by the aforementioned transforms with more structured embeddings $-$ such as compositions of randomized Hadamard transforms $-$ while retaining the same embedding dimension.
  In this paper, we introduce two constructions based on a composition of randomized Hadamard transforms, albeit with a Gaussian rather than Rademacher diagonal in the second stage. The first adds Gaussian dithering to smooth the quantizer, while the second inserts a random permutation to regularize the covariance structure of the resulting Gaussian measurements.
  We prove embedding-dimension and running-time guarantees analogous to those of Fast JL in the non-quantized setting. The first construction achieves $m=O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log^2(d/δ))$, while the second achieves $m=O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log(d/δ))$ under a restriction on $m$. Both constructions can be applied in $O(d\log d)$ time.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: A Tight Bound for Facial Distance Patterns in Planar Graphs
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Let $G$ be an undirected unweighted planar graph and let $S=(s_0,\dots,s_{k-1})$ be the vertices of a designated face, listed in cyclic order. Consider a vector that stores the distances from an arbitrary vertex $v$ to all vertices of $S$. The pattern of $v$ is obtained by taking the difference between every pair of consecutive values in this vector. Li and Parter [STOC'19] proved an upper bound of $O(k^3)$ on the number of unique patterns over all vertices of $G$. We improve this to $O(k^2)$, matching a known lower bound and settling a conjecture in [ISAAC'22]. The simple proof was found by OpenAI's GPT 5.6-Sol model. Plugging this new bound into known results has the following three immediate implications for undirected unweighted planar graphs: (1) it gives an improved compression of the Okamura-Seymour metric (2) it improves the space required by constant-time exact distance oracles, and (3) it improves the fastest distributed algorithm for computing the diameter. We further present a previously unknown and nontrivial implication: a (centralized) $\tilde{O}(n^{8/5})$-time algorithm for computing the diameter, improving over the $\tilde{O}(n^{5/3})$ algorithm of [SODA'18] which works for weighted directed planar graphs. Thus, there is currently a gap between the time for computing the diameter between weighted and unweighted planar graphs.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Bootstrapping Classical and Quantum Query Lower Bounds for Finding Tarski Fixed Points
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
The Tarski fixed-point problem asks for a fixed point of a monotone map on a $k$-dimensional grid lattice of width $n$ and has applications in game theory, economics, and verification. Substantial gaps remain between the known upper and lower bounds on its quantum query complexity.
  We prove two hardness bootstrapping theorems for quantum query lower bounds. Starting from a hard instance family whose instances have pair-wise incomparable unique fixed points, and a lower bound established by the nonnegative adversary method, we bootstrap this lower bound by (i) a factor of $Ω(t)$ when the dimension is multiplied by $t$ and the width remains unchanged, and (ii) a factor of $Ω(\log m)$ when the width is multiplied by $m$ and the dimension is doubled. Applying these theorems, we obtain three consequences: (i) an $Ω(k\log^2 n)$ lower bound for $k\geq 4$, improving previously best-known classical and quantum lower bounds; (ii) for every fixed constant $α>0$, there exists a constant $δ(α)>0$ such that $Q_ε(\text{Tarski}(n,k))=Ω(kn^{δ(α)})$ whenever $k>n^α$, and in particular, an $Ω(kn^{0.0072})$ lower bound for $k>n^{2/203}$, the first lower bound with simultaneous linear dependence on the dimension and polynomial dependence on the width; and (iii) a superpolynomial lower bound of $(k/\log k)^{Ω(\log k)}$ for exponentially wide grids, where $n=2^{Θ(k)}$. The last result rules out a route to polynomial-time algorithms for simple stochastic games and ARRIVAL through generic polynomial-query black-box Tarski solvers.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Hashrope: A Persistent Data Structure for Mechanisms of LLM Context Management
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Serving stacks for large language models manage context through four recurring mechanisms: incremental edits to a growing context, branching and snapshotting for tree search, identification of reusable prefixes for KV-cache reuse, and encoding of repeated segments. Each mechanism is served today by a different specialist structure. We show that all four reduce to a single persistent weight-balanced rope whose every node carries a polynomial hash of its subtree over a Mersenne prime, so that the structure supports logarithmic edits and logarithmic verified content-identity queries at the same time. We validate each mechanism with pre-registered, replicated experiments, then compare against a deployed specialist per mechanism: the Ropey editing library, a faithful PagedAttention copy-on-write block table, and the vendored SGLang radix matcher. On workloads that interleave edits with identity queries, Hashrope is net-superior to Ropey by a factor that grows without bound (369.7x at one million characters). Against the radix matcher on a live vLLM stack serving Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M on four A100 GPUs, Hashrope identifies a one-million-token shared prefix exactly and 1.20x faster, at a context length the dense engine cannot even prefill.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Conjunctive Queries with Negation: Beyond Signed-Acyclicity
Approximation algorithms via discrepancy with hard constraints
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
In this paper, we present a discrepancy-based approach to cost-preserving rounding under hard constraints. Starting from a feasible fractional solution, our rounding procedure preserves the designated hard constraints, never increases the linear objective, and bounds the error in the remaining constraints by the discrepancy of a suitable column-difference matrix.
  Our second discrepancy-theoretic result bounds the discrepancy of a matrix in terms of a novel column parameter, called mountain distance. This notion captures ordered structural features of a matrix which are invisible to the classical Beck--Fiala and Komlós column-norm parameters.
  We show a variety of applications of these two results. In particular, we obtain new results for min-cost unsplittable flows, bounded-turn routing in grids and tori, rainbow prefix hypergraph decomposition, and $2$-multicast scheduling.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Improved Approximations for Coflow Scheduling via Iterated Rounding and Stable Matchings
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We study Coflow Scheduling, introduced by Chowdhury, Zhong, and Stoica (2014). We give deterministic polynomial-time algorithms achieving a $2.77$-approximation without release dates and a $3.17$-approximation with integer release dates. These improve the $3.42$ and $4.36$ guarantees of Rohwedder and Schnaars (2025).
  Our approach combines two ideas: (1) a novel iterated rounding scheme, and (2) Galvin's list edge coloring method, which is based on the Gale--Shapley stable matching algorithm.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Online Submodular Welfare Maximization: Computation is not the Bottleneck
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We revisit the online submodular welfare maximization problem (OSW), a vast generalization of numerous well-studied online allocation problems, including online bipartite matching, display ads and AdWords. A natural greedy OSW algorithm achieves a competitive ratio of $1/2$ [LLN06], and $1-1/e$ under i.i.d. arrivals [KPV13]. Both bounds are tight for polynomial-time algorithms unless NP=RP [KPV13]. The information-theoretic limits for OSW, in contrast, remained open. This prompted researchers to ask for tighter upper bounds [Mehta13] or conjecture the existence of better-competitive (slow) algorithms [Huang23, LTX+23, CHS24, Huang2024, HTW24}.
  We resolve Mehta's question and refute the subsequent conjectures, proving that the greedy algorithm is in fact tight for both adversarial and i.i.d. arrivals, regardless of computation time. Seemingly contradicting recent $(1-1/e)$-competitive fractional algorithms for OSW [HJP+24,Patton26], we show that this impossibility even holds for fractional algorithms, provided their outputs correspond to marginals that are roundable in hindsight. Conceptually, our proofs can be seen as identifying that a bottleneck for OSW, even under (deterministic) adversarial arrivals, is the inherently random notion of correlation gap [ADSY12].

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Stochastic Weighted Caching with Per-Request Predictions
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
Both the unweighted and weighted variants of caching are cornerstone problems in competitive analysis, with tight randomized competitive ratios of $Θ(\log k)$, where $k$ is the cache size. We study weighted caching with per-request predictions, where each page request is accompanied by a prediction of the next arrival time of the same page. For unweighted caching, such perfect predictions suffice to implement Belady's offline optimal rule. For weighted caching, however, previous work shows that a logarithmic lower bound persists even with perfect predictions on adversarial request sequences. Stochastic assumptions alone are also insufficient: the classical caching lower bounds already apply to uniform independent requests. In this work, we ask whether combining these two sources of additional information can overcome this barrier, and answer this question affirmatively.
  Specifically, we develop an efficient, deterministic cache eviction policy that achieves a competitive ratio of $15.75$ using perfect per-request predictions when page requests are drawn independently from an arbitrary, known static distribution in every step, and page costs are arbitrary. Our algorithm's performance degrades gracefully under erroneous predictions: we prove a bound of $O(\min\{1+E,\log k\})$ on the competitive ratio, where $E$ aggregates each page's average prediction error, and may be unknown to the algorithm.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: QPTAS for Max Weight Independent Set in Graphs with Strongly Edge-Sublinear Separators
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: A hereditary graph class has strongly edge-sublinear separators if, for some constant $0 \leqslant b < 1$, every graph in the class with $m$ edges admits a balanced separator of size $\mathcal O(m^b)$. We show that Max Weight Independent Set (MWIS) admits a deterministic quasipolynomial-time approximation scheme (QPTAS) on every such class. In particular, this applies to graphs excluding any fixed graph as an induced minor, by a separator theorem of Korhonen and Lokshtanov [SODA 2024]. Our theorem generalizes the QPTASes for axis-parallel rectangles [Adamaszek and Wiese, FOCS 2013] and polygons [Adamaszek, Har-Peled, and Wiese, JACM 2019], or equivalently for packing connected subgraphs of a planar graph [Pilipczuk, van Leeuwen, and Wiese, Algorithmica 2020]. It also generalizes the QPTAS for MWIS on hereditary classes with strongly sublinear separators measured in vertices [Dvořák, EJC 2018; Dvořák and Lahiri, ESA 2021], as well as the QPTASes for graphs excluding particular induced minors [Chudnovsky et al., arXiv 2025; Bonnet et al., SWAT 2026; Czyżewska et al., arXiv 2026].

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Online Batching with Lookahead: Adversarial Limits and Stochastic Gains
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
Modern inference systems rely on batching to exploit parallel execution and amortize serial execution overheads, but batching creates a fundamental online scheduling tradeoff: serving requests immediately reduces request queuing delay, while waiting can form larger batches that better utilize parallel hardware and improve serving efficiency. We study this tradeoff in a single-server online batching model with bounded batch capacity, fixed batch processing time, and the objective of minimizing total flow time. Our focus is on the value of finite lookahead into future arrivals over a purely online setting for scheduling.
  We show that the benefits of lookahead depend on the arrival model. In the adversarial setting, finite perfect lookahead has inherent limitations: for any bounded lookahead window, every online algorithm remains separated from the offline optimum by a constant factor. Thus, worst-case arrival sequences can prevent perfect knowledge of future events from fully overcoming online uncertainty. In contrast, under Poisson arrivals in the stable regime, finite lookahead is much more powerful. Although the best distribution-aware online algorithm has a nonzero asymptotic gap from the offline optimum, lookahead closes this gap exponentially fast in the window length. We prove matching upper and lower bounds up to constants in the exponent. Together, these results give a tight characterization of when lookahead can close the online--offline gap, incorporating insights from the competitive analysis of online algorithms into queueing-theoretic steady-state bounds.
  We also study imperfect predictions, showing that the benefit of lookahead degrades gracefully with prediction error. Simulations on synthetic arrivals and experiments on real request traces support the theory: modest lookahead substantially reduces flow time and brings online batching close to the offline benchmark.

Graphics.title: HoOPOE: A Holography-Optimized Perceptual ObjectivE function
Graphics.summary: Holographic devices must reconstruct an entire light field given a finite number of spatial light modulator (SLM) pixels, and must do so using scalar-wave diffraction from coherent illumination alone. As a result, computer-generated holography (CGH) often has speckling artifacts. We propose HoOPOE (Holography-Optimized Perceptual ObjectivE function), a CGH-specific, perceptually-aware loss function that hides speckles from human vision. HoOPOE is effective for CGH optimizations because it accounts for the human visual system's sensitivity to spatio-temporal frequencies and color, and its parameters are tuned to maximize its performance as a loss function for CGH. We use HoOPOE to generate holograms for mesh-derived focal stacks. We then conduct a user study to benchmark HoOPOE-generated holograms against existing loss functions. HoOPOE yields the most visually pleasing results; users prefer HoOPOE 68% of the time over the next best objective function on average.

Graphics.title: SplatBus: A Gaussian Splatting Viewer Framework via GPU Interprocess Communication
Graphics.summary: Radiance field-based rendering methods have attracted significant interest from the computer vision and computer graphics communities.
